A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProactiveBench study. The main text, tables, figures, mathematical content, and appendices A–H are readable and support comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of MLLMs, prompting and action-distribution analyses, and reinforcement-learning experiments, with additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports multi-turn open-ended generation results in Table 10.

M1.justification: Benchmark construction, environment actions, and GRPO training with the same reward choices remain unchanged. The added multi-turn open-ended experiment extends the evaluation protocol rather than modifying the trained models.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven datasets and scenarios, with QuickDraw and COCO supplying training data. The additional multi-turn open-ended evaluation reuses this coverage.

E2.justification: Model membership is unchanged in the retained MCQA, single-turn open-ended, reference, and hinted comparisons. The new multi-turn experiment evaluates 12 models already represented in the existing suite; it introduces no new baseline method.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 adds a supplementary multi-turn open-ended protocol that maps inapplicable suggestions to random valid actions and measures trajectory accuracy and intervention rate. This replaces the earlier cross-format comparison using aggregate accuracy. The original evaluation settings remain.

E4.justification: v2 examines whether weak open-ended performance persists with multiple interaction turns. Appendix A.8 also adds a modeled recall comparison for filtering thresholds. Existing invalid-action, hint, history, few-shot, and reward analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix A.8 adds binomial-based recall estimates: 92.8% for the chosen filtering rule versus 37.6% for a binomial-test alternative at a 0.05 threshold, assuming 40% first-turn success. Neither version reports experimental confidence intervals or repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: The MCQA aggregate results in v1 Table 10 are removed and replaced by multi-turn open-ended results for 12 models. Qwen2.5-VL-7B leads the new comparison with 3.9% accuracy and 0.1 intervention rate. These are different-protocol results, not performance changes. Retained numerical tables and single-turn component scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.8 introduces binomial-model reasoning under an assumed 40% success probability to justify the six-of-22 filtering cutoff. v1 supplied empirical filtering curves without this mathematical rationale. The MDP formulation and training reward rules remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: current models lack proactiveness, prompting provides limited benefits, and reinforcement learning can improve proactiveness with transfer to unseen scenarios.

C2.justification: v2 more explicitly distinguishes frequent suggestions from successful proactive behavior and explains why single-turn OEG and MCQA metrics are not directly comparable. Results sections narrow the scaling statement to no simple monotonic relationship within tested families. Appendix A.8 adds arguments about filtering-pool dependence and future evaluation.

D1.justification: Filtering documentation explicitly identifies first-turn MCQA predictions, the six-of-22 cutoff, and the pool spanning ten model families. These clarify the existing procedure. Training hyperparameters, hardware, runtime information, prompts, and code/data access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 72 works and retain the same positioning relative to MLLM benchmarks and active vision. Reference formatting and bibliographic metadata changes do not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify metrics, interpretations, and filtering. Terminology distinguishes MCQA intervention rate from OEG suggestion percentages; affiliations and keywords are also updated. The main section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively retypeset with a narrower text block, different typography and headers, and widespread resizing and relocation of displays. Table 2 now separates category and suggestion scores, Figure 6c displays suggestion percentages instead of aggregate accuracy, and Table 10 presents a different experiment.

improvement.justification: Separating suggestion frequency from successful answering makes the findings easier to interpret, and the new multi-turn comparison adds relevant evidence. The gain is limited: core results are unchanged, the earlier MCQA aggregate comparison is removed, and the replacement relies on approximate action substitution. The added filtering rationale is also assumption-dependent.
